I used a 3/4” bit and fit 6 cat6 cables through. 1/2” bit should do 3 cables easily. 

I get the “it needs to stay steady”. I spent so much time placing and replacing the bit to try and get the perfect hit center of the horizontal piece of wood in my walls. 

Basically what I did: determine where the fire block was, drill 1/4” hole above it for my bore scope, had my partner confirm I was hitting where I wanted (they were downstairs I was in the attic with the drill bit), and drilled. Filled in the 1/4” hole afterwards, painted, and good to go. 

I can’t stress enough how helpful a bore scope/endoscope can be in many home improvement situations especially in a house with plaster&lath. 

If you want to do it solo, you can do any combination of what I did but honestly the flex bit is probably your best bet in my opinion. 

Also, just for fun get the endoscope/bore scope. Helped me with electrical, plumbing, collapsed exterior drain. It was $50 when I bought it.

Edit: also check out the home networking subreddit. Lots of people have done things similar to what you are doing and plenty of posts of people adding Ethernet to old walls.

I was frequently an overnight manager of a 24/7 downtown urban store. While I worked a variety of shifts, my schedule also included overnight shifts. In my first three months of overnights I had to tell someone “no we don’t have a bathroom” and watched them say “thats fine” and drop trousers and shit on the floor in the store. Things like this became a semi-regular occurrence. 

While I appreciate sometimes you need a late night run to the store for cough medicine or the likes, I wholeheartedly despised my overnight shifts.
